skills.name: The significance of the laws of thought

note.text: The classical laws help keep reasoning stable and detect incompatible claims. Their use requires care with meaning, time and conditions. Identity discourages equivocation: using one word with different meanings as if it were unchanged. Non-contradiction exposes claims that cannot hold together under the same conditions. Excluded middle concerns P and its exact negation, not any pair of opposite-sounding words. Unknown does not mean false; neither does disagreement by itself settle the facts.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: The classical laws help keep reasoning stable and detect incompatible claims. Their use requires care with meaning, time and conditions. Identity discourages equivocation: using one word with different meanings as if it were unchanged. Non-contradiction exposes claims that cannot hold together under the same conditions. Excluded middle concerns P and its exact negation, not any pair of opposite-sounding words. Unknown does not mean false; neither does disagreement by itself settle the facts.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A notice says the Bamenda club meeting is cancelled. Another says it is not cancelled for the same meeting at the same time. The class should check the date and source rather than accept both unchanged. If a second notice concerns next week's meeting, the statements may be compatible. Precision prevents unnecessary disputes.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Restate both claims using the same terms. Match their times and subjects. Ask whether one is genuinely the negation of the other. If information is missing, suspend judgment and investigate. Logical rules organise evidence; they do not supply the missing timetable or observe the meeting for us.

key_words.meaning: switching a word's meaning within reasoning
claims that negate one another under the same conditions
denial of the same proposition rather than a different claim
withholding a decision when evidence is insufficient

examples: A learner moves from saving at a bank to sitting on a river bank as though bank meant the same thing.
The same meeting is cancelled and the same meeting is not cancelled.
The denial of the room is open now is the room is not open now.

mistake.wrong: Repeating the same spelling guarantees the same meaning.
mistake.right: equivocation: switching a word's meaning within reasoning.
mistake.why: One spelling can have different meanings; this switch breaks the reasoning.
